For nearly two years, I’ve been losing weight and dealing with mysterious digestive issues (I’ll spare you the gory details). I went to Dr. Kahn expecting at least a conversation about my blood results. What I got instead? A cheerful dismissal because “everything looks normal.”

His golden advice? “Eat more sugar” and, wait for it… “Try Yakult.” Yes, Yakult. The sugary supermarket yogurt drink with 20g of sugar per shot—suddenly elevated to probiotic gold in Dr. Kahn’s world. Apparently, that’s what decades of experience boils down to: pushing processed sugar drinks as gut health solutions.

Needless to say, I left the appointment more baffled than helped. I chose to listen to my body (since my doctor clearly wasn’t interested) and sought a private second opinion. Lo and behold: diagnosed with H. pylori and a stuck-open ileocecal valve. Both real, treatable issues. Both completely ignored.

What’s most disappointing? I explained how much this was affecting my life—and got absolutely nothing back but indifference. I’m not sure what’s worse: the lack of curiosity or the lack of care
